papers.title: Higher SARS-CoV-2 infection burden among racialized individuals: evidence from Canadian serology data
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: COVID-19 infection risk has not been evenly distributed across racial groups, with exposure being shaped by social and structural factors. The emergence of highly transmissible variants (i.e., Omicron) dramatically increased infection rates. However, it remains unclear whether racial disparities in infection risk disappeared or persisted over the course of the pandemic. OBJECTIVE: To understand how SARS-CoV-2 infection risk differed between racial groups in Canada and whether those disparities changed with the Omicron variant. METHODS: We analyzed cross-sectional SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence data from the Canadian Blood Services serosurveillance program (June 2020 to April 2023) using a previously described dynamic susceptible-infection model, while accounting for seroreversion. Race-specific force of infection was estimated for the pre-Omicron and Omicron periods (with the emergence of Omicron defined as beginning December 26, 2021). RESULTS: Prior to Omicron, racialized individuals had a 121% higher force of infection (IRR = 2.205; 95% CI: 2.115-2.299). During the Omicron period, infection rates rose significantly within each racial group relative to the pre-Omicron period, with a 55.52-fold increase among White individuals and a 31.27-fold increase among racialized individuals. Despite this, racialized individuals remained disproportionately affected following the emergence of Omicron, with 24% higher infection rates than those of their White counterparts (IRR = 1.242; 95% CI: 1.231-1.253). CONCLUSION: Widespread infection during Omicron did not result in epidemiologic equity, as racialized populations continued to experience higher infection risk despite crude seroprevalence depicting convergence.

papers.title: Investigating respiratory infection as a post-COVID-19 condition using a large passive surveillance cohort from Track PCC.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: This study examined risk factors for post-COVID respiratory infection using data from the Tracking the Burden, Distribution, Impact of Tracking Post-COVID-19 Conditions in Diverse Populations for Children, Adolescents, Adults (Track PCC) passive surveillance cohort. METHODS: This retrospective study included adult Temple Health patients in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania with SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) infections from March 2020 to December 2022 and ≥ 90 days follow-up. COVID-19 infection was identified via laboratory testing, billing codes, or clinical documentation. The primary outcome was post-COVID respiratory infection identified by billing codes. Predictors included social, clinical, and COVID-related correlates. Adjusted logistic regression models were used on 17,539 complete cases and multiple imputed datasets (n = 45,513) with SuperMICE. RESULTS: In complete-case analysis, uninsured coverage, Alpha variant, total comorbidities, and hospitalization were associated with lower odds of respiratory post-COVID conditions (ORs: 0.02-0.99). Dual Medicare/Medicaid and current smokers, increased odds (ORs: 1.33-1.58). Imputed analyses showed consistent results with and additionally observed higher odds of respiratory infection among those with Medicaid and higher number of vaccinations, and lower odds among those of any non-white race, Hispanic ethnicity. CONCLUSIONS: Temple Track PCC findings identify high-risk populations and underscore the utility of advanced imputation in surveillance-based research.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection include persistent respiratory symptoms, but risk factors for post-COVID respiratory infection remain incompletely characterized in diverse populations. This study addressed a knowledge gap on social and clinical correlates of post-COVID respiratory infection using a large passive surveillance cohort.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the Track PCC passive surveillance system among adult patients from Temple Health in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, with SARS-CoV-2 infection from March 2020 to December 2022 and at least 90 days of follow-up.
analysis.methods: SARS-CoV-2 infection was identified via laboratory testing, billing codes, or clinical documentation. The primary outcome was post-COVID respiratory infection identified by billing codes. Predictors included social, clinical, and COVID-related correlates. Adjusted logistic regression models were applied to 17,539 complete cases and multiple imputed datasets (n = 45,513) using SuperMICE.
analysis.main_results: In complete-case analysis, uninsured coverage, Alpha variant, total comorbidities, and hospitalization were associated with lower odds of respiratory post-COVID conditions (ORs: 0.02–0.99). Dual Medicare/Medicaid and current smokers showed increased odds (ORs: 1.33–1.58). Imputed analyses confirmed these findings and additionally found higher odds among those with Medicaid and higher number of vaccinations, and lower odds among those of any non-white race or Hispanic ethnicity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study identifies specific high-risk populations for post-COVID respiratory infection and demonstrates the utility of advanced imputation methods in enhancing surveillance-based research validity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings can inform targeted surveillance, risk stratification, and clinical follow-up strategies for individuals at higher risk of post-COVID respiratory complications.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on passive surveillance data and billing codes, which may introduce misclassification and residual confounding, limiting causal inference. Evidence strength is moderate due to retrospective design and reliance on administrative data.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective cohort study from Temple Health in Philadelphia examined risk factors for post-COVID respiratory infection using the Track PCC passive surveillance system among adults with SARS-CoV-2 infection from March 2020 to December 2022. papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: This study examined risk factors for post-COVID respiratory infection using data from the Tracking the Burden, Distribution, Impact of Tracking Post-COVID-19 Conditions in Diverse Populations for Children, Adolescents, Adults (Track PCC) passive surveillance cohort. METHODS: This retrospective study included adult Temple Health patients in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania with SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) infections from March 2020 to December 2022 and ≥ 90 days follow-up. COVID-19 infection was identified via laboratory testing, billing codes, or clinical documentation. The primary outcome was post-COVID respiratory infection identified by billing codes. Predictors included social, clinical, and COVID-related correlates. Adjusted logistic regression models were used on 17,539 complete cases and multiple imputed datasets (n = 45,513) with SuperMICE. RESULTS: In complete-case analysis, uninsured coverage, Alpha variant, total comorbidities, and hospitalization were associated with lower odds of respiratory post-COVID conditions (ORs: 0.02-0.99). Dual Medicare/Medicaid and current smokers, increased odds (ORs: 1.33-1.58). Imputed analyses showed consistent results with and additionally observed higher odds of respiratory infection among those with Medicaid and higher number of vaccinations, and lower odds among those of any non-white race, Hispanic ethnicity. CONCLUSIONS: Temple Track PCC findings identify high-risk populations and underscore the utility of advanced imputation in surveillance-based research.

papers.title: Association of COVID-19 vaccination with improved treatment adherence in patients with schizophrenia: A propensity score-matched cohort study
papers.abstract: People with schizophrenia are a high-priority group for COVID-19 vaccination. However, large-scale data on the real-world clinical impact of vaccination in this vulnerable population is limited. We aimed to evaluate the association of COVID-19 vaccination with treatment adherence, psychiatric stability, and SARS-CoV-2 infection risk in patients with schizophrenia. We conducted a nationwide, retrospective, propensity score-matched cohort study (study period: December 1, 2019-December 31, 2022) using linked data from the National Health Insurance Service and Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency databases in South Korea. We identified patients with schizophrenia aged 19-64 years and stratified them into vaccinated (three doses) and unvaccinated groups. A 1:1 propensity score matching was performed. The primary outcomes were schizophrenia-related hospitalization and emergency department visits. Key secondary outcomes included medication adherence and diagnosed SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study cohort comprised 4629 pairs (N = 9258). No significant between-group differences were observed in the rates of schizophrenia-related hospitalization or emergency department visits. The vaccinated group showed a significantly smaller decline in medication adherence compared with the unvaccinated group. Counter-intuitively, the vaccinated group had a significantly higher rate of diagnosed SARS-CoV-2 infection, a finding most plausibly attributable to ascertainment bias rather than reduced vaccine efficacy. COVID-19 vaccination was not associated with psychiatric destabilization but was associated with significantly improved treatment adherence. Our study indicates that vaccination may play a supportive role in maintaining clinical continuity for individuals with schizophrenia.

papers.title_zh: COVID-19 疫苗接种与精神分裂症患者治疗依从性改善的关联:倾向评分匹配队列研究
papers.source_body_en: People with schizophrenia are a high-priority group for COVID-19 vaccination. However, large-scale data on the real-world clinical impact of vaccination in this vulnerable population is limited. We aimed to evaluate the association of COVID-19 vaccination with treatment adherence, psychiatric stability, and SARS-CoV-2 infection risk in patients with schizophrenia. We conducted a nationwide, retrospective, propensity score-matched cohort study (study period: December 1, 2019-December 31, 2022) using linked data from the National Health Insurance Service and Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency databases in South Korea. We identified patients with schizophrenia aged 19-64 years and stratified them into vaccinated (three doses) and unvaccinated groups. A 1:1 propensity score matching was performed. The primary outcomes were schizophrenia-related hospitalization and emergency department visits. Key secondary outcomes included medication adherence and diagnosed SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study cohort comprised 4629 pairs (N = 9258). No significant between-group differences were observed in the rates of schizophrenia-related hospitalization or emergency department visits. The vaccinated group showed a significantly smaller decline in medication adherence compared with the unvaccinated group. Counter-intuitively, the vaccinated group had a significantly higher rate of diagnosed SARS-CoV-2 infection, a finding most plausibly attributable to ascertainment bias rather than reduced vaccine efficacy. COVID-19 vaccination was not associated with psychiatric destabilization but was associated with significantly improved treatment adherence. Our study indicates that vaccination may play a supportive role in maintaining clinical continuity for individuals with schizophrenia.

papers.title: Physical activity in social contexts during the COVID-19 pandemic: a latent transition analysis
papers.abstract: Background While physical activity behaviours have been explored during the COVID-19 pandemic, little is known about the social contexts in which physical activity took place during this time of crisis. The purpose of this longitudinal study was to explore the physical activity-related social contexts in which young people (aged 15-24) engaged during the first two years of the COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario, Canada. Specific objectives included identifying: (1) how patterns of engagement in social contexts changed over time; and (2) demographic/descriptive predictors of social context-related class membership. Methods Online surveys were completed from: (1) July-September 2020; (2) November 2020-January 2021; and (3) July 2021-January 2022. Data on gender, living situation, physical activity, and physical activity-related social contexts were collected. Latent transition analysis was conducted to determine how participant's social contexts changed over time and chi-squared tests were used to assess predictors of latent profile membership. Results Participants (n = 328; M age = 22.95) were categorized into three latent classes: 1 = mainly active alone; 2 = limited physical activity in all contexts; and 3 = mainly active with others. At Time 1, nearly 70.0% of participants were in Class 1; at Times 2 and 3, most participants (62.1% and 53.6%, respectively) were in Class 2. From Times 1-2, most participants (67.1%) transitioned from Class 1 to Class 2. From Times 2-3, more than 75.0% of participants remained in their respective classes. Class membership was associated with various predictors at different time points. Conclusion Results underscore the need to promote participation in a variety of physical activity-related social contexts, particularly during times of crisis.

papers.title: The COVID-19 Pandemic and Changes in Cancer Screening Disparities from 2015 to 2023: An NSHAP Survey Study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND From 1990 to 2020, cancer screening rates in the United States steadily rose, but disparities persisted. Cancer screening was disrupted by the COVID-19 pandemic, possibly worsening disparities. OBJECTIVE We utilized a longitudinal cohort of age-eligible adults to examine pre-pandemic (2015-16) and late-pandemic (2021-23) cancer screening rates to evaluate health disparities. DESIGN This is a study of participants who completed National Social Life, Health, and Aging Project (NSHAP) surveys in 2015-16 and 2021-23. We used univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses to measure differences by age, gender, race and ethnicity, education level, marital status, and income in screening for colorectal, prostate and breast cancer. PARTICIPANTS We studied data from 2,585 NSHAP participants who completed both surveys. MAIN MEASURES Self-reported past-year colorectal, breast, and prostate cancer screening rates completed with colonoscopies, mammograms, and prostate-specific antigen (PSA) testing, respectively. KEY RESULTS The proportion of respondents completing colonoscopies, mammograms, and PSA testing did not change across surveys. Younger individuals (aged < 60) had lower mammogram rates in 2015-16 (52.8% vs. 62.9%, p = 0.04) and lower PSA testing in both surveys (37.0% vs. 53.5%, p < 0.001 and 34.3% vs. Hispanic respondents had the lowest colonoscopy screening rates in 2015-16 (12.1%, p = 0.006) and 2021-23 (7.6%, p = 0.002), and Black women had the highest for mammograms in 2015-16 (65.3%, p = 0.04). Non-partnered men had lower PSA testing than partnered men in both surveys (p = 0.02 and p = 0.005). All screening rates were lower for those with lower incomes in 2015-16 (p < 0.05 for all). Analyses did not show significant demographic differences in screening rates over time. CONCLUSIONS Overall population cancer screening rates remained consistent from 2015-16 to 2021-23. Demographic differences in cancer screening rates persisted, with no subgroups disproportionately affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. Targeted outreach is needed for demographic subgroups such as Hispanic individuals with persistently low colorectal cancer screening rates.

Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to measure differences by age, gender, race and ethnicity, education level, marital status, and income (A5).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Overall population cancer screening rates remained consistent from 2015-16 to 2021-23, with no significant change in the proportion of respondents completing colonoscopies, mammograms, and PSA testing across surveys (A8, A16). analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed cancer screening rates among 2,585 age-eligible adults in the United States during the pre-pandemic (2015-16) and late-pandemic (2021-23) periods. However, demographic disparities persisted, with Hispanic individuals showing the lowest colorectal cancer screening rates and Black women having the highest mammogram rates. No subgroups were disproportionately affected by the COVID-19 pandemic, and targeted outreach is recommended for groups with persistently low screening rates.

analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该研究并未显示随时间推移筛查率存在显着的人口统计学差异 (A15),而且 COVID-19 大流行对筛查差异的具体影响仍不清楚,因为没有哪个亚组受到不成比例的影响 (A17)。证据没有报告差异持续存在的具体机制或原因(A12、A14)。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 需要针对人口亚群进行有针对性的推广,例如结直肠癌筛查率持续较低的西班牙裔个人 (A18)。

papers.title: Health-related quality of life profiles and trajectories of patients with post COVID-19 condition: a latent Markov model.
papers.abstract: Background The aim of this study was to identify subgroups with similar health states based on health-related quality of life (HRQoL) profile (i.e. differences in affected dimensions and severity of problems per dimension) among PCC patients, to examine transitions between these subgroups over time, and to examine the association with sociodemographic and medical characteristics. Methods In this longitudinal cohort study, data from 5,737 PCC patients, collected through two online surveys, were analysed using a latent Markov model. Dichotomized HRQoL scores per EQ-5D-5L dimension were used as indicators to determine latent states and covariates were added into the model. Results A model with six latent states was selected. The largest state, consisting of 31% of respondents, was characterized by a high probability of problems on all dimensions, whereas the smallest state (7%) was characterized by a low probability of problems on all dimensions, except usual activities. The remaining four states were all characterized by a high probability of problems on usual activities and pain/discomfort, but differed based on the probability of problems on the dimensions mobility, self-care and anxiety/depression. The probability of transitioning to a different state was low, with states with fewer affected dimensions being most stable. Women, younger respondents, those with a lower educational level, and those with comorbidity were more likely to be in states with more affected dimensions. Conclusions The identification of different HRQoL profiles shows that there is substantial heterogeneity in the HRQoL dimensions that are affected and in observed changes between two measurement points.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景 本研究的目的是根据 PCC 患者的健康相关生活质量 (HRQoL) 概况(即受影响维度和每个维度问题严重程度的差异)来识别具有相似健康状况的亚组,检查这些亚组之间随时间的转变,并检查与社会人口学和医学特征的关联。方法 在这项纵向队列研究中,使用潜在马尔可夫模型对通过两次在线调查收集的 5,737 名 PCC 患者的数据进行了分析。每个 EQ-5D-5L 维度的二分 HRQoL 分数用作确定潜在状态的指标,并将协变量添加到模型中。结果选择了具有六个潜在状态的模型。最大的州(由 31% 的受访者组成)的特点是在所有维度上出现问题的概率都很高,而最小的州(7%)的特点是除了日常活动之外,在所有维度上出现问题的概率都很低。其余四种状态的特征都是在日常活动和疼痛/不适方面出现问题的可能性很高,但在活动能力、自我护理和焦虑/抑郁方面出现问题的概率有所不同。转换到不同状态的概率很低,受影响维度较少的状态最稳定。女性、年轻受访者、教育水平较低的受访者以及患有合并症的受访者更有可能处于受影响程度更大的州。结论 不同 HRQoL 概况的识别表明,受影响的 HRQoL 维度以及两个测量点之间观察到的变化存在显着的异质性。

papers.title: Community-Engaged Respondent-Driven Sampling: The California Pacific Islander Well-Being and COVID-19 Economic Survey, 2024.
papers.abstract: To describe how community engagement combined with respondent-driven sampling (RDS) enabled timely documentation of the mental health and socioeconomic impacts of COVID-19 on California's Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander (NHPI) adult population. The California Pacific Islander Well-Being and COVID-19 Economic Survey (CAPIWAVES) was a collaboration between NHPI community-based organizations and academic researchers who sampled 929 NHPI adults in California from January to May 2024. The initial respondents were composed of a convenience sample of 58 CHamoru, Fijian, Marshallese, Native Hawaiian, Sāmoan, and Tongan respondents in Northern, Central, and Southern California, who referred up to 4 others. Compared with the American Community Survey, CAPIWAVES RDS estimates differed. We reported initial data findings to NHPI community members in June 2024 in an online webinar. In April 2025, we released a report with the analyzed CAPIWAVES data, with community-generated recommendations for policy, programming, and research. Although data were not population-representative, community-engaged RDS was an efficient method for collecting and disseminating needed data for minoritized populations. ( Am J Public Health . Published online ahead of print July 16, 2026:e1-e12. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308517).

papers.title: Epidemics and Nigerian Society: Lessons from Smallpox to COVID-19
papers.abstract: Nigeria's struggle with epidemic disease, from colonial-era smallpox campaigns to the COVID-19 pandemic, provides a century-long record of how a society has navigated between biomedical intervention and lived social experience. Historical and contemporary disease outbreaks in Nigeria are rarely studied as a connected sequence. Scholarship isolates each epidemic within its own disciplinary environment, distorting patterns of governance, culture, and social response that repeat across time. This paper addressed that challenge through a comparative historical analysis of four epidemic moments in Nigeria which are smallpox and other pre-contemporary epidemics such as, HIV/AIDS, the 2014 Ebola outbreak, and COVID-19. The paper draws on colonial and postcolonial health records, government and multilateral reports, and peer-reviewed literature. It traced how institutional legacies, public trust in the state, and cultural frameworks of illness have redefined each successive epidemic. The analysis found a strong path dependency which is are mechanisms improvised during the smallpox and polio campaigns. On the other hand, community engagement, traditional leadership, decentralized surveillance, reemerged as decisive factors behind Nigeria's most effective interventions. Notable among this was the Ebola containment, while their erosion correlates with weaker outcomes in the HIV/AIDS and COVID-19 responses. The paper closes with recommendations for repositioning community-centred, culturally literate governance into Nigeria's epidemic preparedness strive.

papers.abstract_zh: 尼日利亚与流行病的斗争,从殖民时代的天花运动到 COVID-19 大流行,提供了一个世纪以来社会如何在生物医学干预和生活社会经验之间导航的记录。尼日利亚历史上和当代的疾病爆发很少被作为一个相互关联的序列来研究。学术将每种流行病隔离在其自身的学科环境中,扭曲了随时间重复出现的治理、文化和社会反应模式。本文通过对尼日利亚的四个流行病时刻(天花和其他前当代流行病,例如艾滋病毒/艾滋病、2014 年埃博拉疫情和 COVID-19)进行比较历史分析来应对这一挑战。该论文借鉴了殖民时期和后殖民时期的健康记录、政府和多边报告以及同行评审的文献。它追溯了制度遗产、公众对国家的信任以及疾病的文化框架如何重新定义了每一次连续的流行病。分析发现,存在很强的路径依赖性,这是天花和脊髓灰质炎运动期间临时建立的机制。另一方面,社区参与、传统领导、分散监控重新成为尼日利亚最有效干预措施背后的决定性因素。其中值得注意的是埃博拉病毒的遏制,而其侵蚀与艾滋病毒/艾滋病和 COVID-19 应对措施的疲软结果相关。该文件最后提出了将以社区为中心、具有文化素养的治理重新定位到尼日利亚流行病防范工作中的建议。

papers.title: The CCR2 inflammatory pathway is a target for improving severe disease and pulmonary inflammation in experimental COVID-19
papers.abstract: Abstract SARS-CoV2 can induce an acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), provoked by a dysregulated hyper-inflammatory pulmonary immune response. Here we used the keratinocyte-18 humanized angiotensin converting enzyme-2 (K18-hACE2) mouse model of SARS-CoV2, where expression of the CoV2 spike protein receptor, hACE-2, is restricted to epithelia, to characterize inflammatory pulmonary immune responses post-intranasal infections with the delta isolate SARS-CoV2(Δ B.1.617.2). Immune-profiling by focused transcript analysis, inflammatory protein array, and multi-color flow cytometry, confirmed that clinically relevant markers of COVID-19 (IL-6, GM-CSF, neutrophils, inflammatory monocytes) were significantly elevated in lungs of mice at day 5 post-infection and that remdesivir anti-viral active metabolite (GS441524) treatment significantly modified SARS-CoV2Δ viral loads and pulmonary-specific inflammation. Chemokine ligands of CCR2 (CCL2/7/8) were amongst the top 5% upregulated pulmonary transcripts in a focused human infection response array to SARS-CoV2Δ. CCL2 was confirmed as elevated in protein assays in SARS-CoV2Δ infected lungs. To address functional relevance of the CCR2 pathway of inflammatory cell recruitment to the lungs mediating disease, mice were administered with anti-CCR2 antibody daily at point of infection for up to six days. Anti-CCR2 treated mice showed significant improved welfare scores, were protected from weight loss, modified myeloid pneumonitis, and displayed significantly blunted cytokine and chemokine response in the lungs, despite not affecting pulmonary viral loads. Our data supports therapeutic benefit of modifying CCR2-dependent cell recruitment in the treatment of viral-induced ARDS.

Here, we used the keratinocyte-18 humanized angiotensin converting enzyme-2 (K18-hACE2) mouse model of SARS-CoV2, where expression of the CoV2 spike protein receptor, hACE-2, is restricted to epithelia, to characterize inflammatory pulmonary immune responses post-intranasal infections with the delta isolate SARS-CoV2( ∆ ) B.1.617.2. Immune-profiling by focused transcript analysis, inflammatory protein array, and multi-color flow cytometry, confirmed that clinically relevant markers of COVID-19 (IL-6, GM-CSF, neutrophils, inflammatory monocytes) were significantly elevated in lungs of mice at day 5 post-infection and that remdesivir antiviral active metabolite (GS441524) treatment significantly modified SARS-CoV2 ∆ viral loads and pulmonary inflammation. Chemokine ligands of CCR2 (CCL2/7/8) were among the top 5% upregulated pulmonary transcripts in a focused human infection response array to SARS-CoV2 ∆ . CCL2 was confirmed as elevated in protein assays in SARS-CoV2 ∆ infected lungs. To address the functional relevance of the CCR2 pathway of inflammatory cell recruitment to the lungs mediating disease, mice were administered with anti-CCR2 antibody daily at the point of infection for up to 6 d. Anti-CCR2 treated mice showed significant improved welfare scores, were protected from weight loss, modified myeloid pneumonitis, and displayed significantly blunted cytokine and chemokine response in the lungs, despite not affecting pulmonary viral loads. Our data supports therapeutic benefit of modifying CCR2-dependent cell recruitment in the treatment of viral-induced ARDS.

elements_zh.main_results: 抗CCR2治疗的小鼠表现出显着改善的福利评分,免受体重减轻和改良性骨髓性肺炎的影响,并且显示出肺部细胞因子和趋化因子反应显着减弱,尽管不影响肺部病毒载量。

papers.title: Herpesvirus reactivation is associated with mortality in critically ill ICU patients with COVID-19: Insights from a retrospective single-center analysis of 455 cases
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Critically ill patients with COVID-19 frequently develop viral reactivation, yet the clinical significance of herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) and cytomegalovirus (CMV) remains a matter of debate. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-center study of 455 consecutive intensive care unit (ICU) patients with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection between March 2020 and December 2021. Patients underwent screening for HSV-1 and CMV in whole blood and respiratory samples. A multivariable model was used to independently investigate risk factors associated with mortality. RESULTS: The mean age was 57 years (range: 13-94 years), and 316 (69%) were male. During a median ICU stay of 14 (0-90) days, viral reactivation (either HSV-1 or CMV or both) occurred in 164 (36%) patients. HSV-1 and CMV co-reactivation was detected in 57 (13%) patients, isolated HSV-1 reactivation was observed in 54 (12%) patients and isolated CMV reactivation in 53 (12%) patients. Median time from ICU admission to viral detection was 4 days, with a stepwise increase with longer ICU stay. Detection of HSV-1 was associated with decreased ICU survival (32% versus 67%; p < 0.001) which remained significant after multivariable adjustment. Detection of HSV-1 but not CMV was associated with an increased need for invasive mechanical ventilation, veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation therapy, and the need for renal replacement therapy. Higher neutrophil-lymphocyte ratios were independently associated with an increased risk of ICU mortality and correlated with detection of HSV-1 and CMV. CONCLUSION: Herpesvirus reactivation was common in critically ill patients with COVID-19. HSV-1 reactivation was associated with a more severe course of disease and increased ICU mortality.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:患有 COVID-19 的危重患者经常出现病毒再激活,但 1 型单纯疱疹病毒 (HSV-1) 和巨细胞病毒 (CMV) 的临床意义仍然存在争议。方法:我们对 2020 年 3 月至 2021 年 12 月期间连续 455 名确诊 SARS-CoV-2 感染的重症监护病房 (ICU) 患者进行了一项回顾性单中心研究。患者在全血和呼吸道样本中接受了 HSV-1 和 CMV 筛查。使用多变量模型独立调查与死亡率相关的危险因素。结果:平均年龄为 57 岁(范围:13-94 岁),其中 316 名(69%)为男性。在 ICU 住院时间中位数 14 (0-90) 天期间,164 名 (36%) 患者发生病毒再激活(HSV-1 或 CMV 或两者)。在 57 名 (13%) 患者中检测到 HSV-1 和 CMV 共同再激活,在 54 名 (12%) 患者中观察到单独 HSV-1 再激活,在 53 名 (12%) 患者中观察到单独 CMV 再激活。从入住 ICU 到病毒检测的中位时间为 4 天,并且随着 ICU 停留时间的延长而逐步增加。HSV-1 检测与 ICU 生存率下降相关(32% 对比 67%;p < 0.001),多变量调整后这一情况仍然显着。HSV-1(而非 CMV)的检测与有创机械通气、静脉-静脉体外膜氧合治疗以及肾脏替代治疗的需求增加相关。较高的中性粒细胞-淋巴细胞比率与 ICU 死亡风险增加独立相关,并与 HSV-1 和 CMV 检测相关。结论:疱疹病毒再激活在 COVID-19 危重患者中很常见。HSV-1 重新激活与更严重的病程和 ICU 死亡率增加相关。

papers.title: Institutional quality and pandemic resilience: cross-country evidence on health and economic outcomes during COVID-19.
papers.abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic exposed large cross-country differences in mortality, vaccination rollout, and economic recovery. We examine whether stronger pre-pandemic institutions were associated with better pandemic performance and whether vaccination rollout helps explain part of that relationship. We combine 2019 World Bank Worldwide Governance Indicators with COVID-19 outcomes, policy measures, World Development Indicators, and V-Dem electoral democracy data, estimating cross-country regressions and a temporally ordered exploratory mediation model using vaccination by September 2021 and deaths accrued in the fourth quarter of 2021. Results In full multivariable specifications, a one-unit increase in the WGI composite is associated with 384 fewer reported COVID-19 deaths per million, 1,860 fewer excess deaths per million, and 15.5% points higher full vaccination coverage by end-2021. These associations remain in robustness checks using V-Dem electoral democracy controls, WGI principal-component measures, timing-specific outcomes, and influence diagnostics. Institutional quality is not robustly associated with GDP growth in 2020; its positive association with GDP growth in 2021 persists but is weaker after controlling for OxCGRT economic-support policies. The exploratory mediation decomposition is consistent with an indirect path through vaccination representing about 35% of the total association between institutional quality and late-2021 mortality. Conclusions Pre-pandemic institutional quality was consistently associated with pandemic health outcomes and vaccine deployment, while economic associations were more phase-specific. The findings are observational and should not be read as definitive causal estimates, but they underscore the relevance of governance capacity for future pandemic preparedness.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 背景 COVID-19 大流行暴露了死亡率、疫苗接种推广和经济复苏方面的巨大跨国差异。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 提供的证据没有明确说明研究设计、设置或研究人群。
elements_zh.methods: 我们将 2019 年世界银行全球治理指标与 COVID-19 结果、政策措施、世界发展指标和 V-Dem 选举民主数据相结合,利用 2021 年 9 月之前的疫苗接种情况和 2021 年第四季度的死亡人数来估计跨国回归和按时间排序的探索性调解模型。

papers.title_zh: 机构质量和大流行抵御能力:关于 COVID-19 期间健康和经济结果的跨国证据。
papers.source_body_en: Background The COVID-19 pandemic exposed large cross-country differences in mortality, vaccination rollout, and economic recovery. We examine whether stronger pre-pandemic institutions were associated with better pandemic performance and whether vaccination rollout helps explain part of that relationship. We combine 2019 World Bank Worldwide Governance Indicators with COVID-19 outcomes, policy measures, World Development Indicators, and V-Dem electoral democracy data, estimating cross-country regressions and a temporally ordered exploratory mediation model using vaccination by September 2021 and deaths accrued in the fourth quarter of 2021. Results In full multivariable specifications, a one-unit increase in the WGI composite is associated with 384 fewer reported COVID-19 deaths per million, 1,860 fewer excess deaths per million, and 15.5% points higher full vaccination coverage by end-2021. These associations remain in robustness checks using V-Dem electoral democracy controls, WGI principal-component measures, timing-specific outcomes, and influence diagnostics. Institutional quality is not robustly associated with GDP growth in 2020; its positive association with GDP growth in 2021 persists but is weaker after controlling for OxCGRT economic-support policies. The exploratory mediation decomposition is consistent with an indirect path through vaccination representing about 35% of the total association between institutional quality and late-2021 mortality. Conclusions Pre-pandemic institutional quality was consistently associated with pandemic health outcomes and vaccine deployment, while economic associations were more phase-specific. The findings are observational and should not be read as definitive causal estimates, but they underscore the relevance of governance capacity for future pandemic preparedness.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景 COVID-19 大流行暴露了死亡率、疫苗接种推广和经济复苏方面的巨大跨国差异。我们研究了更强大的大流行前机构是否与更好的大流行表现相关,以及疫苗接种的推出是否有助于解释这种关系的部分原因。我们将 2019 年世界银行全球治理指标与 COVID-19 结果、政策措施、世界发展指标和 V-Dem 选举民主数据相结合,估计跨国回归和使用截至 2021 年 9 月疫苗接种的临时有序探索性调解模型以及 2021 年第四季度累计的死亡人数。结果在完整的多变量规范中,WGI 综合数据每增加一个单位,报告的死亡人数就会减少 384 人。到 2021 年底,每百万人的 COVID-19 死亡人数、每百万人的超额死亡人数减少 1,860 人,全面疫苗接种覆盖率提高 15.5%。使用 V-Dem 选举民主控制、WGI 主成分测量、特定时间结果和影响力诊断,对这些关联进行稳健性检查。制度质量与 2020 年 GDP 增长并不存在显着相关性;它与 2021 年 GDP 增长的正相关仍然存在,但在控制 OxCGRT 经济支持政策后,其正相关减弱。探索性中介分解与疫苗接种的间接路径一致,约占机构质量与 2021 年末死亡率之间总关联的 35%。结论 大流行前的机构质量始终与大流行健康结果和疫苗部署相关,而经济关联则更具阶段性。这些发现是观察性的,不应被解读为明确的因果估计,但它们强调了治理能力与未来大流行防范的相关性。

papers.title: Clinical characteristics and predictors of severe pertussis in hospitalized children after the COVID-19 period in Türkiye: a multicenter study.
papers.abstract: Pertussis resurged globally, after the relaxation of COVID-19 measures, underscoring its continued relevance as a public health concern, yet data remain limited on the factors associated with severe disease in children. The present study identified risk factors for severe pertussis to improve early recognition and clinical management. This multicenter retrospective study analyzed the demographic, clinical, and laboratory data of the 839 children hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed pertussis across 47 centers in Türkiye (2023-2024). Severe disease was defined as the need for respiratory support or the development of encephalopathy and/or cardiovascular dysfunction. After univariate comparison, significant variables were evaluated using center-adjusted multivariable logistic regression in vaccine-eligible (> 2 months) and non-eligible (≤ 2 months) groups. The patient's median age was 2 months (IQR 1.5-5.0), and 77.8% were younger than 6 months. Severe disease occurred in 26.1% of cases. In univariate analysis, younger age, vaccine refusal, refugee status, feeding difficulties, apnea, respiratory distress, leukocytosis, viral co-infection, and abnormal chest X-ray findings at admission were associated with severe disease. In infants ≤ 2 months, apnea (OR = 3.74; p 3 /μL increase; p = 0.003) were independently associated with severe disease. In children > 2 months, respiratory distress (OR = 13.59; p < 0.001) and not being up-to-date with vaccination (OR = 2.60; p = 0.019) were independent predictors of severe disease. Overall, 21.5% of patients required intensive care, 24.3% needed ventilation, and mortality was 2.4%. Conclusion: Severe pertussis predominantly affects young infants, and apnea, respiratory distress, and leukocytosis were identified as major predictors of severe disease. Furthermore, incomplete vaccination is associated with increased disease severity.

papers.title: COVID-19 and temporal perception: prolonged short-term time perception in a post-pandemic world
papers.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has profoundly restructured daily life, significantly impacting mental health. This negative event has been reported to alter subjective experience of time, such as the blending of days, reflecting distortions in long-term time perception over relatively coarse scales. However, the influence of the COVID-19 pandemic on short-term time perception over fine scales has received much less attention. Here we delve into this underexplored territory, demonstrating that the pandemic, as a high-arousal negative event, lengthens our perception of short time intervals. Using a two-session duration discrimination paradigm, we showed that COVID-19 related images were perceived as significantly longer than neutral pictures of the same duration. Unlike emotion-induced temporal distortions, this dilation was consistent across sessions, correlated with heightened arousal, remained unaffected by anxiety, and exhibited a long-lasting effect - persisting even four years after the initial outbreak. Taken together, our findings highlight a temporal dilation induced by COVID-19 stimuli, extending our understanding of how high-arousal negative events interact with cognitive processes, particularly time perception.

papers.title: The Resurgence of Respiratory Viruses After COVID-19: Molecular Insights from Pediatric SARI in Kashmir.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory viruses are major contributors to severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) in children. Data on their molecular epidemiology in northern India remains limited, particularly in the post-COVID-19 period. This study aimed to determine the prevalence and distribution of respiratory viral pathogens among hospitalized pediatric SARI patients in Kashmir. METHODS: A prospective study was conducted from October 2023 to April 2025 at Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences, Srinagar. Children aged ≤15 years meeting the World Health Organization SARI case definition were enrolled. Nasopharyngeal and/or oropharyngeal samples were collected and tested using real-time polymerase chain reaction assays for SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A and B, Respiratory Syncytial virus (RSV) A and B, Adenovirus, Human metapneumovirus, Rhinovirus, and Para-influenza viruses. RESULTS: A total of 326 pediatric SARI cases were included. At least one respiratory virus was detected in 200 patients (61.3%). RSV was the most frequently detected virus, with RSV-B identified in 111 cases (34.0%) and RSV-A in 26 cases (7.9%). Influenza viruses accounted for a smaller proportion, including influenza A(H1N1) in 12 cases (3.6%), influenza A(H3N2) in 6 cases (1.8%), and influenza B (Victoria lineage) in 21 cases (6.4%). Other viruses detected included Adenovirus, Para-influenza virus, Rhinovirus, and Human metapneumovirus. Most infections occurred during winter months and predominantly affected infants. CONCLUSION: Respiratory viruses account for a substantial proportion of pediatric SARI cases in Kashmir, with RSV emerging as the predominant pathogen in the post-pandemic period. Strengthening molecular surveillance may improve diagnostic stewardship and guide targeted prevention strategies.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:呼吸道病毒是儿童严重急性呼吸道感染(SARI)的主要原因。印度北部的分子流行病学数据仍然有限,特别是在后 COVID-19 时期。本研究旨在确定克什米尔住院儿童 SARI 患者中呼吸道病毒病原体的患病率和分布。方法:2023 年 10 月至 2025 年 4 月在斯利那加谢尔克什米尔医学科学研究所进行了一项前瞻性研究。纳入符合世界卫生组织SARI病例定义的年龄≤15岁的儿童。收集鼻咽和/或口咽样本,并使用实时聚合酶链反应检测 SARS-CoV-2、甲型和乙型流感、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) A 和 B、腺病毒、人类偏肺病毒、鼻病毒和副流感病毒。结果:共纳入 326 例儿童 SARI 病例。200 名患者(61.3%)中至少检测到一种呼吸道病毒。RSV 是最常检测到的病毒,其中 RSV-B 在 111 例(34.0%)中检出,RSV-A 在 26 例(7.9%)中检出。流感病毒所占比例较小,其中甲型H1N1流感12例(3.6%),甲型H3N2流感6例(1.8%),乙型流感(维多利亚系)21例(6.4%)。检测到的其他病毒包括腺病毒、副流感病毒、鼻病毒和人类偏肺病毒。大多数感染发生在冬季,主要影响婴儿。结论:克什米尔儿童 SARI 病例中呼吸道病毒占很大比例,RSV 成为大流行后时期的主要病原体。加强分子监测可以改善诊断管理并指导有针对性的预防策略。

papers.title: Durability and Breadth of Neutralizing Antibodies Against SARS-CoV-2 Variants Following XBB.1.5 Vaccination in a Multiply Exposed Cohort
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Widespread immunity from vaccination and infection has reduced COVID-19 morbidity and mortality, but this immunity varies across the population. Understanding how repeated antigenic exposures influence antibody responses helps to inform future vaccination strategies. Methods We characterized neutralizing antibody responses in serum samples collected one and six months after XBB.1.5 vaccination from 25 healthcare workers with varying, complex histories of vaccination and reported infections. Neutralizing activity was assessed against a range of variants, from pre-Omicron to recent Omicron JN.1 sublineage, and divergent BA.3.2 variants using lentiviral pseudoviruses. Participants were stratified into five exposure groups based on their documented vaccination and reported infection history. Results XBB.1.5 vaccination elicited broad neutralizing responses, with strong boosting against previously encountered antigens relative to vaccine-matched XBB.1.5 and newer variants. Geometric mean neutralization titers were generally comparable across exposure groups, though small subgroup sizes and considerable intra-group heterogeneity precluded definitive conclusions about the influence of prior exposure history. At six months, titers declined by 36-62% across all variants. Titers remained highest against pre-Omicron variants and were lowest against JN.1 sublineage variants, with some falling to very low levels. Conclusions In this cohort with extensive prior antigenic exposures, broad neutralizing antibody profiles were observed following XBB.1.5 vaccination, though these responses waned substantially after six months. The observed waning of cross-neutralizing antibodies against emerging variants underscores the challenge of maintaining durable protection and supports the need for continued monitoring of antibody responses to guide evidence-based updates to COVID-19 vaccines.

papers.title_zh: 在多次暴露队列中接种 XBB.1.5 疫苗后针对 SARS-CoV-2 变体的中和抗体的持久性和广度
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Widespread immunity from vaccination and infection has reduced COVID-19 morbidity and mortality, but this immunity varies across the population. Understanding how repeated antigenic exposures influence antibody responses helps to inform future vaccination strategies. Methods We characterized neutralizing antibody responses in serum samples collected one and six months after XBB.1.5 vaccination from 25 healthcare workers with varying, complex histories of vaccination and reported infections. Neutralizing activity was assessed against a range of variants, from pre-Omicron to recent Omicron JN.1 sublineage, and divergent BA.3.2 variants using lentiviral pseudoviruses. Participants were stratified into five exposure groups based on their documented vaccination and reported infection history. Results XBB.1.5 vaccination elicited broad neutralizing responses, with strong boosting against previously encountered antigens relative to vaccine-matched XBB.1.5 and newer variants. Geometric mean neutralization titers were generally comparable across exposure groups, though small subgroup sizes and considerable intra-group heterogeneity precluded definitive conclusions about the influence of prior exposure history. At six months, titers declined by 36-62% across all variants. Titers remained highest against pre-Omicron variants and were lowest against JN.1 sublineage variants, with some falling to very low levels. Conclusions In this cohort with extensive prior antigenic exposures, broad neutralizing antibody profiles were observed following XBB.1.5 vaccination, though these responses waned substantially after six months. The observed waning of cross-neutralizing antibodies against emerging variants underscores the challenge of maintaining durable protection and supports the need for continued monitoring of antibody responses to guide evidence-based updates to COVID-19 vaccines.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 对疫苗接种和感染的广泛免疫力降低了 COVID-19 的发病率和死亡率,但这种免疫力因人群而异。了解重复的抗原暴露如何影响抗体反应有助于为未来的疫苗接种策略提供信息。方法 我们对 XBB.1.5 疫苗接种后 1 个月和 6 个月收集的血清样本中的中和抗体反应进行了表征,这些样本来自 25 名具有不同且复杂的疫苗接种史和报告感染史的医护人员。使用慢病毒假病毒评估了一系列变体的中和活性,从前 Omicron 到最近的 Omicron JN.1 亚系,以及不同的 BA.3.2 变体。根据参与者记录的疫苗接种情况和报告的感染史,将其分为五个暴露组。结果 XBB.1.5 疫苗接种引发了广泛的中和反应,相对于疫苗匹配的 XBB.1.5 和更新的变体,对先前遇到的抗原具有强烈的增强作用。尽管较小的亚组规模和相当大的组内异质性排除了关于既往暴露史的影响的明确结论,但几何平均中和滴度在不同暴露组之间通常具有可比性。六个月时,所有变体的滴度下降了 36-62%。针对 Omicron 前变体的滴度仍然最高,针对 JN.1 亚系变体的滴度最低,其中一些下降到非常低的水平。结论 在这个先前广泛接触过抗原的队列中,在 XBB.1.5 疫苗接种后观察到了广泛的中和抗体谱,尽管这些反应在六个月后大幅减弱。观察到的针对新兴变种的交叉中和抗体的减弱凸显了维持持久保护的挑战,并支持持续监测抗体反应的必要性,以指导基于证据的 COVID-19 疫苗更新。

papers.title: Identifying severe COVID-19 risk variants modulating enhancer reporter activity in lung cells
papers.abstract: Common genetic variants contribute to risk for complex human diseases. However, despite thousands of associations, variants modulating disease risk and their functional impact remain largely unknown. This includes SARS-CoV-2 infection, where outcomes range from asymptomatic to fatal. Most genetic risk variants associated with COVID-19 disease, identified through genome wide association studies, are located in the non-coding genome and may function by altering gene expression in disease-relevant cells and tissues. To address this at scale, we tested >4800 severe COVID-19-associated variants to determine the impact of individual variants and variant combinations on regulatory activity using Self-Transcribing Active Regulatory Region sequencing, a massively-parallel reporter assay. Focusing on variants that may have their impact in the lung, in a lung epithelial cell line (A549) we identify 166 variants within active sequences, of which 29 modulate activity allele-specifically. Evaluating variant combinations, we observe both additive and non-additive effects on regulatory activity. We employ state-of-the-art deep learning models to interpret allele-specific variant effects on regulatory activity and endogenous genomic features. Our work provides a set of prioritised severe COVID-19-associated variants that modulate regulatory activity in lung epithelial cells, candidate transcription factors, and candidate target genes with potential to be disease modifying.

papers.title_zh: 识别调节肺细胞增强子报告活性的严重 COVID-19 风险变异
papers.source_body_en: Common genetic variants contribute to risk for complex human diseases. However, despite thousands of associations, variants modulating disease risk and their functional impact remain largely unknown. This includes SARS-CoV-2 infection, where outcomes range from asymptomatic to fatal. Most genetic risk variants associated with COVID-19 disease, identified through genome wide association studies, are located in the non-coding genome and may function by altering gene expression in disease-relevant cells and tissues. To address this at scale, we tested >4800 severe COVID-19-associated variants to determine the impact of individual variants and variant combinations on regulatory activity using Self-Transcribing Active Regulatory Region sequencing, a massively-parallel reporter assay. Focusing on variants that may have their impact in the lung, in a lung epithelial cell line (A549) we identify 166 variants within active sequences, of which 29 modulate activity allele-specifically. Evaluating variant combinations, we observe both additive and non-additive effects on regulatory activity. We employ state-of-the-art deep learning models to interpret allele-specific variant effects on regulatory activity and endogenous genomic features. Our work provides a set of prioritised severe COVID-19-associated variants that modulate regulatory activity in lung epithelial cells, candidate transcription factors, and candidate target genes with potential to be disease modifying.
papers.abstract_zh: 常见的遗传变异会增加复杂人类疾病的风险。然而,尽管存在数千种关联,但调节疾病风险的变异及其功能影响仍然很大程度上未知。这包括 SARS-CoV-2 感染,其后果从无症状到致命不等。通过全基因组关联研究鉴定出的大多数与 COVID-19 疾病相关的遗传风险变异位于非编码基因组中,可能通过改变疾病相关细胞和组织中的基因表达来发挥作用。为了大规模解决这个问题,我们使用自转录活性调节区测序(一种大规模并行报告分析)测试了超过 4800 个严重的 COVID-19 相关变异,以确定单个变异和变异组合对监管活动的影响。着眼于可能对肺产生影响的变异,在肺上皮细胞系 (A549) 中,我们鉴定了活性序列内的 166 个变异,其中 29 个特异性调节等位基因活性。通过评估变体组合,我们观察到对监管活动的加性和非加性影响。我们采用最先进的深度学习模型来解释等位基因特异性变异对调控活动和内源基因组特征的影响。我们的工作提供了一组优先的严重 COVID-19 相关变体,这些变体调节肺上皮细胞、候选转录因子和候选靶基因的调节活性,有可能改变疾病。

papers.title: Covid-19 related excess mortality: An analysis by age for selected countries
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Measures of excess mortality are generally regarded as providing the best metric for countries' experience during the Covid pandemic of 2020-2022. Such measures, however, need to be adjusted to take account of the different age structures of different countries as Covid-related mortality can differ substantially by age. METHODS: This paper analyses excess mortality data for a selection of countries using the Short Term Mortality Fluctuations dataset. A standardised age distribution is applied to the data to obtain age-adjusted excess mortality and this is compared to crude excess mortality data. The metric of years of life lost (YLL) is also calculated for the same dataset and cluster analysis is applied to investigate relationships between the mortality metrics and GDP per capita and inequality. RESULTS: The age adjustment makes a significant difference for some countries but the overall ranking of countries in terms of excess mortality changes very little, with rank correlation coefficients in excess of 0.95 for the metrics of crude mortality, age adjusted mortality and YLL Age adjusted excess mortality has a rank correlation of -0.69 with GDP per capita but the rank correlation with the Gini coefficient of 0.11 is not statistically significant. CONCLUSIONS: Rankings of countries by excess mortality during the Covid period are robust to age adjustment and choice of mortality metric. Cluster analysis suggests distinct clusterings of countries with similar outcomes, particularly the former planned economies of central and eastern Europe.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzes excess mortality data for selected countries during the Covid-19 pandemic, adjusting for age differences to provide a more accurate comparison. Using the Short Term Mortality Fluctuations dataset, the study applies a standardised age distribution to calculate age-adjusted excess mortality and compares it to crude excess mortality data. Additionally, the metric of years of life lost (YLL) is calculated, and cluster analysis is applied to investigate relationships between mortality metrics and GDP per capita and inequality. The results show that age adjustment significantly affects excess mortality rankings for some countries, but overall rankings change very little, with high rank correlation coefficients for crude mortality, age-adjusted mortality, and YLL. Age-adjusted excess mortality has a strong negative correlation with GDP per capita but a non-significant correlation with the Gini coefficient. The study concludes that rankings of countries by excess mortality are robust to age adjustment and choice of mortality metric, with distinct clusterings of countries with similar outcomes, particularly former planned economies of central and eastern Europe. The findings suggest that age-adjusted excess mortality rankings are reliable indicators of countries' experiences during the pandemic, which can inform public health strategies and resource allocation. The study is limited to a selection of countries and relies on the Short Term Mortality Fluctuations dataset, which may not be fully representative. The evidence strength is moderate due to the abstract-only evidence and the specific dataset used.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 超额死亡率被认为是评估各国在 Covid-19 大流行期间经历的最佳指标,但由于与年龄相关的死亡率不同,这些指标需要根据各国的年龄差异进行调整。本研究旨在分析和比较选定国家的年龄调整超额死亡率数据。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用短期死亡率波动数据集分析了一些国家的超额死亡率数据,应用标准化年龄分布来获得年龄调整后的超额死亡率,并将其与粗略的超额死亡率数据进行比较。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用短期死亡率波动数据集,并应用标准化年龄分布来计算年龄调整的超额死亡率,然后与粗略的超额死亡率数据进行比较。此外,还计算了寿命损失年数 (YLL) 指标,并应用聚类分析来研究死亡率指标与人均 GDP 和不平等之间的关系。
elements_zh.main_results: 年龄调整对一些国家的超额死亡率排名产生显着影响,但总体排名变化很小,粗死亡率、年龄调整死亡率和 YLL 的排名相关系数超过 0.95。年龄调整超额死亡率与人均GDP的相关性为-0.69,但与基尼系数0.11的相关性并不具有统计显着性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究发现,Covid-19期间死亡率过高的国家排名对于年龄调整和死亡率指标的选择来说是稳健的,具有相似结果的国家有明显的集群,特别是中欧和东欧的前计划经济体。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,按年龄调整的超额死亡率排名是各国在 Covid-19 大流行期间经历的可靠指标,可以为公共卫生战略和资源分配提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于选定的国家,并依赖于短期死亡率波动数据集,该数据集可能不完全具有代表性。由于仅摘要证据和使用的特定数据集,证据强度中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:超额死亡率的衡量标准通常被认为是衡量各国在 2020-2022 年新冠大流行期间经历的最佳指标。然而,这些措施需要进行调整,以考虑到不同国家不同的年龄结构,因为与新冠病毒相关的死亡率可能因年龄而有很大差异。方法:本文使用短期死亡率波动数据集分析了一些国家的超额死亡率数据。将标准化年龄分布应用于数据以获得年龄调整的超额死亡率,并将其与粗略的超额死亡率数据进行比较。还针对同一数据集计算了生命损失年数 (YLL) 指标,并应用聚类分析来研究死亡率指标与人均 GDP 和不平等之间的关系。结果:年龄调整对一些国家有显着差异,但国家超额死亡率的总体排名变化很小,粗死亡率、年龄调整死亡率和YLL年龄调整超额死亡率指标的等级相关系数均超过0.95,与人均GDP的等级相关性为-0.69,但与基尼系数0.11的等级相关性不具有统计显着性。结论:新冠疫情期间死亡率过高的国家排名对于年龄调整和死亡率指标的选择来说是稳健的。聚类分析表明,具有相似结果的国家存在明显的聚类,特别是中欧和东欧的前计划经济体。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 超额死亡率被认为是评估各国在 Covid-19 大流行期间经历的最佳指标,但由于与年龄相关的死亡率不同,这些指标需要根据各国的年龄差异进行调整。本研究旨在分析和比较选定国家的年龄调整超额死亡率数据。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用短期死亡率波动数据集分析了一些国家的超额死亡率数据,应用标准化年龄分布来获得年龄调整后的超额死亡率,并将其与粗略的超额死亡率数据进行比较。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究使用短期死亡率波动数据集,并应用标准化年龄分布来计算年龄调整的超额死亡率,然后与粗略的超额死亡率数据进行比较。此外,还计算了寿命损失年数 (YLL) 指标,并应用聚类分析来研究死亡率指标与人均 GDP 和不平等之间的关系。
analysis_zh.main_results: 年龄调整对一些国家的超额死亡率排名产生显着影响,但总体排名变化很小,粗死亡率、年龄调整死亡率和 YLL 的排名相关系数超过 0.95。年龄调整超额死亡率与人均GDP的相关性为-0.69,但与基尼系数0.11的相关性并不具有统计显着性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究发现,Covid-19期间死亡率过高的国家排名对于年龄调整和死亡率指标的选择来说是稳健的,具有相似结果的国家有明显的集群,特别是中欧和东欧的前计划经济体。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,按年龄调整的超额死亡率排名是各国在 Covid-19 大流行期间经历的可靠指标,可以为公共卫生战略和资源分配提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于选定的国家,并依赖于短期死亡率波动数据集,该数据集可能不完全具有代表性。由于仅摘要证据和使用的特定数据集,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Neurocognitive and psychological symptoms in post COVID-19 patients (PASC24): prospective cohort study protocol.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Knowledge about the late effects of COVID-19, or so-called post-acute sequelae of COVID (PASC), and its pathogenesis is still very limited. The purpose of this observational study is to chart late neurocognitive effects of the COVID-19 infection. The aim is to increase knowledge of the underlying biological processes and describe how biomarkers correlate with degree of symptoms, mapping their role as diagnostic markers over time (24 months). METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This prospective observational cohort study is longitudinal and monitors patients with neurocognitive and psychological symptoms after COVID-19 infection in order to analyse the impact on the brain. For these purposes, we introduce a digital neuropsychological platform (Mindmore). We also aim to analyse potential diagnostic and prognostic markers from blood and cerebrospinal fluid and use MRI of the brain. We will measure the patients' return to work and studies as well as any impact on their ADL functions and quality of life. The ongoing study aims to follow-up to 100 study participants with PASC for 24 months at three visits: baseline, 12 months and 24 months. The findings of the study can be used as guidance for future policy management in healthcare and may lead to a possible curative or symptom-relieving treatment. ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: This study was approved by the Swedish Ethical Review Authority (diary number: 2020-0604 (main application), 2021-03205, 2023-00023-02, 2024-00426-02 (amendments)). Participants will be required to provide informed consent. The results of this study will be reported in peer-reviewed journals and presented at scientific conferences. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT06298006.

papers.abstract_zh: 简介:关于 COVID-19 的后期影响或所谓的 COVID 急性后遗症 (PASC) 及其发病机制的知识仍然非常有限。这项观察性研究的目的是绘制 COVID-19 感染对晚期神经认知的影响。目的是增加对潜在生物过程的了解,并描述生物标志物如何与症状程度相关,随着时间的推移(24 个月)绘制它们作为诊断标志物的作用。方法和分析:这项前瞻性观察性队列研究是纵向的,监测感染 COVID-19 后出现神经认知和心理症状的患者,以分析其对大脑的影响。为此,我们引入了数字神经心理学平台(Mindmore)。我们还旨在分析血液和脑脊液中的潜在诊断和预后标志物,并使用大脑 MRI。我们将衡量患者恢复工作和学习的情况以及对其 ADL 功能和生活质量的影响。正在进行的研究旨在对 100 名接受 PASC 的研究参与者进行为期 24 个月的随访,分 3 次访视:基线、12 个月和 24 个月。该研究的结果可以作为未来医疗保健政策管理的指导,并可能带来可能的治愈或缓解症状的治疗方法。伦理与传播:本研究得到瑞典伦理审查局批准(日记号:2020-0604(主申请)、2021-03205、2023-00023-02、2024-00426-02(修正案))。参与者将被要求提供知情同意。这项研究的结果将在同行评审期刊上报道并在科学会议上展示。试用注册号:NCT06298006。

papers.title: Environmental prevalence of enteric viruses across the covid-19 pandemic: A three-year monitoring study.
papers.abstract: Enteric viruses are continuously excreted in high concentrations in human feces and are disseminated into aquatic environments through treated and untreated wastewater, much of which is ultimately discharged into coastal marine waters. Environmental surveillance of these pathogens may therefore reflect their circulation in human populations and serve as an early-warning tool for the emergence of new viruses or variants, as well as increased transmission of existing ones. In this study, we investigated the occurrence and molecular diversity of major gastroenteric viruses - adenovirus, noroviruses, rotavirus - together with other enteric viruses with variable clinical relevance, in coastal marine waters of Campania Region (Southern Italy). Viral prevalence was evaluated according to season, sampling year, and type of wastewater discharge. A total of 500 marine water samples were collected, of which nearly half (44.0%) tested positive for at least one viral target. Viral detection rates varied across years, presumably influenced by the epidemiological dynamics associated with the COVID-19 pandemic. Notably, phylogenetic analyses revealed that most environmental viral sequences were identical or closely related to strains previously identified in human clinical cases from the same geographical area, supporting a strong epidemiological link between human infections and environmental contamination. Overall, these findings underscore the value of integrated environmental surveillance for public health risk assessment within a One Health framework.

papers.title_zh: covid-19 大流行期间肠道病毒的环境流行率:一项为期三年的监测研究。
papers.source_body_en: Enteric viruses are continuously excreted in high concentrations in human feces and are disseminated into aquatic environments through treated and untreated wastewater, much of which is ultimately discharged into coastal marine waters. Environmental surveillance of these pathogens may therefore reflect their circulation in human populations and serve as an early-warning tool for the emergence of new viruses or variants, as well as increased transmission of existing ones. In this study, we investigated the occurrence and molecular diversity of major gastroenteric viruses - adenovirus, noroviruses, rotavirus - together with other enteric viruses with variable clinical relevance, in coastal marine waters of Campania Region (Southern Italy). Viral prevalence was evaluated according to season, sampling year, and type of wastewater discharge. A total of 500 marine water samples were collected, of which nearly half (44.0%) tested positive for at least one viral target. Viral detection rates varied across years, presumably influenced by the epidemiological dynamics associated with the COVID-19 pandemic. Notably, phylogenetic analyses revealed that most environmental viral sequences were identical or closely related to strains previously identified in human clinical cases from the same geographical area, supporting a strong epidemiological link between human infections and environmental contamination. Overall, these findings underscore the value of integrated environmental surveillance for public health risk assessment within a One Health framework.
papers.abstract_zh: 肠道病毒持续以高浓度从人类粪便中排出,并通过经过处理和未经处理的废水传播到水生环境中,其中大部分最终排入沿海海水。因此,对这些病原体的环境监测可以反映它们在人群中的传播情况,并作为新病毒或变种出现以及现有病毒传播增加的预警工具。在这项研究中,我们调查了坎帕尼亚地区(意大利南部)沿海水域中主要胃肠病毒(腺病毒、诺如病毒、轮状病毒)以及具有不同临床相关性的其他肠道病毒的发生和分子多样性。根据季节、采样年份和废水排放类型评估病毒流行率。总共收集了 500 个海水样本,其中近一半 (44.0%) 的至少一种病毒目标检测呈阳性。病毒检出率多年来有所不同,可能是受到与 COVID-19 大流行相关的流行病学动态的影响。值得注意的是,系统发育分析表明,大多数环境病毒序列与先前在同一地理区域的人类临床病例中鉴定的毒株相同或密切相关,这支持了人类感染与环境污染之间的强大流行病学联系。总体而言,这些发现强调了在“同一个健康”框架内进行综合环境监测对公共卫生风险评估的价值。

papers.title: Nirmatrelvir for acute COVID-19 to prevent long COVID (PANORAMIC Norway): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Long-term symptoms are common after acute COVID-19, particularly fatigue, cognitive problems, and dyspnoea. Cohort studies have suggested that antiviral treatment of acute COVID-19 might prevent development of post-COVID-19 condition (also known as long COVID), but the efficacy of antivirals has yet to be verified in prospective studies. We aimed to investigate whether treatment of acute SARS-CoV-2 infection with nirmatrelvir-ritonavir would reduce the risk of long COVID. METHODS: In this double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial, participants were recruited from the municipal health-care service at three sites in Norway (Bergen, Oslo, and Ålesund). Non-hospitalised adults aged 18-65 years with SARS-CoV-2 infection confirmed by PCR or lateral flow test and symptoms for 5 days or fewer were eligible for inclusion. Key exclusion criteria included pregnancy or lactation, chronic renal impairment or chronic liver dysfunction, and any person judged by the investigator to need nirmatrelvir-ritonavir treatment due to increased risk of hospitalisation or death. Participants were allocated in a 1:1 ratio to receive oral 300 mg nirmatrelvir and 100 mg ritonavir, or placebo, twice a day for 5 days using a pre-generated randomisation list without stratification or block adjustment. Participants, clinicians, and the study team were masked to treatment allocation. The primary outcome was long COVID, defined as patient-reported fatigue, dyspnoea, and/or cognitive symptoms at 3 months' follow-up. Safety was analysed as a secondary outcome, and included adverse events, hospital admissions, and deaths. Both the primary outcome and safety were assessed in the intention-to-treat population. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05852873) and is now closed to new participants. FINDINGS: Between May 12, 2023, and June 11, 2025, we enrolled 144 participants, of whom 66 were assigned to nirmatrelvir-ritonavir and 78 to placebo. In the protocol we planned to enrol 2000 participants, but the trial was stopped prematurely by the steering committee due to insufficient recruitment. Among the 143 participants who completed follow-up, the risk of long COVID at 3 months was significantly reduced in the nirmatrelvir-ritonavir group (17 [26%] of 66) compared with the placebo group (33 [43%] of 77), corresponding to a relative risk after imputation of data for the single missing value in the placebo group of 0·60 (95% CI 0·37-0·98; p=0·039). In the nirmatrelvir-ritonavir group, five patients discontinued treatment due to adverse events. The most common adverse events in the nirmatrelvir-ritonavir group were change in taste or smell (57 [86%] of 66 in the nirmatrelvir-ritonavir group vs 14 [18%] of 78 in the placebo group) and nausea or vomiting (19 [29%] vs eight [10%]). Inversely, palpitations were more common in the placebo group (ten [13%] of 78) than in the nirmatrelvir-ritonavir group (two [3%] of 66). No severe adverse events were reported. INTERPRETATION: Treatment with nirmatrelvir-ritonavir for acute COVID-19 was associated with a significant reduction in the risk of long COVID at 3 months' follow-up. The limited sample size precludes firm conclusions, and further clinical trials are warranted. FUNDING: National Health Authorities' KlinBeForsk programme, Western Norway Regional Health Authority, Helse Møre og Romsdal Hospital Trust, and The Influenza Centre, Haukeland University Hospital and University of Bergen, Bergen, Norway.

Key exclusion criteria included pregnancy or lactation, chronic renal impairment or chronic liver dysfunction, and any person judged by the investigator to need nirmatrelvir-ritonavir treatment due to increased risk of hospitalisation or death. Participants were allocated in a 1:1 ratio to receive oral 300 mg nirmatrelvir and 100 mg ritonavir, or placebo, twice a day for 5 days using a pre-generated randomisation list without stratification or block adjustment. Participants, clinicians, and the study team were masked to treatment allocation. The primary outcome was long COVID, defined as patient-reported fatigue, dyspnoea, and/or cognitive symptoms at 3 months' follow-up. Safety was analysed as a secondary outcome, and included adverse events, hospital admissions, and deaths. Both the primary outcome and safety were assessed in the intention-to-treat population. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05852873) and is now closed to new participants. FINDINGS: Between May 12, 2023, and June 11, 2025, we enrolled 144 participants, of whom 66 were assigned to nirmatrelvir-ritonavir and 78 to placebo. In the protocol we planned to enrol 2000 participants, but the trial was stopped prematurely by the steering committee due to insufficient recruitment. Among the 143 participants who completed follow-up, the risk of long COVID at 3 months was significantly reduced in the nirmatrelvir-ritonavir group (17 [26%] of 66) compared with the placebo group (33 [43%] of 77), corresponding to a relative risk after imputation of data for the single missing value in the placebo group of 0·60 (95% CI 0·37-0·98; p=0·039). In the nirmatrelvir-ritonavir group, five patients discontinued treatment due to adverse events. The most common adverse events in the nirmatrelvir-ritonavir group were change in taste or smell (57 [86%] of 66 in the nirmatrelvir-ritonavir group vs 14 [18%] of 78 in the placebo group) and nausea or vomiting (19 [29%] vs eight [10%]). Inversely, palpitations were more common in the placebo group (ten [13%] of 78) than in the nirmatrelvir-ritonavir group (two [3%] of 66). No severe adverse events were reported. INTERPRETATION: Treatment with nirmatrelvir-ritonavir for acute COVID-19 was associated with a significant reduction in the risk of long COVID at 3 months' follow-up. The limited sample size precludes firm conclusions, and further clinical trials are warranted. FUNDING: National Health Authorities' KlinBeForsk programme, Western Norway Regional Health Authority, Helse Møre og Romsdal Hospital Trust, and The Influenza Centre, Haukeland University Hospital and University of Bergen, Bergen, Norway.

papers.title_zh: Nirmatrelvir 用于治疗急性 COVID-19,以预防长期 COVID(挪威全景):一项双盲、随机、安慰剂对照试验。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Long-term symptoms are common after acute COVID-19, particularly fatigue, cognitive problems, and dyspnoea. Cohort studies have suggested that antiviral treatment of acute COVID-19 might prevent development of post-COVID-19 condition (also known as long COVID), but the efficacy of antivirals has yet to be verified in prospective studies. Key exclusion criteria included pregnancy or lactation, chronic renal impairment or chronic liver dysfunction, and any person judged by the investigator to need nirmatrelvir-ritonavir treatment due to increased risk of hospitalisation or death. Participants were allocated in a 1:1 ratio to receive oral 300 mg nirmatrelvir and 100 mg ritonavir, or placebo, twice a day for 5 days using a pre-generated randomisation list without stratification or block adjustment. Participants, clinicians, and the study team were masked to treatment allocation. The primary outcome was long COVID, defined as patient-reported fatigue, dyspnoea, and/or cognitive symptoms at 3 months' follow-up. Safety was analysed as a secondary outcome, and included adverse events, hospital admissions, and deaths. Both the primary outcome and safety were assessed in the intention-to-treat population. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05852873) and is now closed to new participants. FINDINGS: Between May 12, 2023, and June 11, 2025, we enrolled 144 participants, of whom 66 were assigned to nirmatrelvir-ritonavir and 78 to placebo. In the protocol we planned to enrol 2000 participants, but the trial was stopped prematurely by the steering committee due to insufficient recruitment. Among the 143 participants who completed follow-up, the risk of long COVID at 3 months was significantly reduced in the nirmatrelvir-ritonavir group (17 [26%] of 66) compared with the placebo group (33 [43%] of 77), corresponding to a relative risk after imputation of data for the single missing value in the placebo group of 0·60 (95% CI 0·37-0·98; p=0·039). papers.abstract_zh: 背景:急性 COVID-19 后长期症状很常见,特别是疲劳、认知问题和呼吸困难。队列研究表明,急性 COVID-19 的抗病毒治疗可能会预防 COVID-19 后病情(也称为长期 COVID)的发展,但抗病毒药物的疗效尚未在前瞻性研究中得到验证。我们的目的是研究用尼马曲韦-利托那韦治疗急性 SARS-CoV-2 感染是否会降低长期感染新冠病毒的风险。方法:在这项双盲、随机、安慰剂对照试验中,参与者是从挪威三个地点(卑尔根、奥斯陆和奥勒松)的市卫生保健服务机构招募的。年龄在 18-65 岁、经 PCR 或侧流检测证实感染 SARS-CoV-2 且症状持续 5 天或更短的非住院成年人有资格纳入。主要排除标准包括妊娠或哺乳、慢性肾功能不全或慢性肝功能障碍,以及研究者判断因住院或死亡风险增加而需要尼马曲韦-利托那韦治疗的任何人。参与者按照 1:1 的比例分配,接受口服 300 mg nirmatrelvir 和 100 mg ritonavir 或安慰剂,每天两次,持续 5 天,使用预先生成的随机列表,无需分层或区组调整。参与者、临床医生和研究团队对治疗分配情况不知情。主要结局是长期新冠肺炎,定义为患者在 3 个月随访时报告的疲劳、呼吸困难和/或认知症状。安全性作为次要结果进行分析,包括不良事件、住院和死亡。主要结局和安全性均在意向治疗人群中进行了评估。该试验已在 ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05852873) 注册,现已不对新参与者开放。调查结果:2023 年 5 月 12 日至 2025 年 6 月 11 日期间,我们招募了 144 名参与者,其中 66 名被分配到尼尔马瑞韦-利托那韦组,78 名被分配到安慰剂组。在方案中,我们计划招募 2000 名参与者,但由于招募不足,试验被指导委员会提前停止。在完成随访的 143 名参与者中,与安慰剂组(77 人中的 33 人 [43%])相比,尼尔马韦-利托那韦组(66 人中的 17 人 [26%])在 3 个月时长期感染新冠病毒的风险显着降低,相当于安慰剂组中单个缺失值数据插补后的相对风险为 0·60(95% CI 0·37-0·98;p=0·039)。在尼尔马瑞韦-利托那韦组中,有 5 名患者因不良事件而停止治疗。尼马曲韦-利托那韦组最常见的不良事件是味觉或嗅觉变化(尼马曲韦-利托那韦组 66 例中有 57 例 [86%],安慰剂组 78 例中有 14 例 [18%])和恶心或呕吐(19 例 [29%] 比 8 例 [10%])。相反,心悸在安慰剂组(78 人中的 10 人 [13%])比尼马瑞韦-利托那韦组(66 人中的 2 人 [3%])更常见。没有报告严重不良事件。解释:在 3 个月的随访中,用尼马曲韦-利托那韦治疗急性 COVID-19 与长期感染 COVID 的风险显着降低相关。有限的样本量无法得出确切的结论,需要进一步的临床试验。资金来源:国家卫生当局的 KlinBeForsk 计划、挪威西部地区卫生局、Helse Møre og Romsdal 医院信托基金、流感中心、Haukeland 大学医院和挪威卑尔根卑尔根大学。

papers.title: Nanopore-Mediated Assembly Enables Precise and Continuous Synthesis of mRNA-Encapsulated Lipid Nanoparticles for COVID-19 Vaccines.
papers.abstract: RNA therapeutics are reshaping modern medicine, as exemplified by the rapid deployment of lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-based mRNA vaccines during the COVID-19 pandemic. However, the ability to reproducibly generate LNPs with precisely defined physicochemical properties at scale remains a critical challenge, particularly as the particle size and size distribution strongly influence biodistribution, cellular uptake, and therapeutic efficacy. Conventional mixing technologies ensure reproducibility but offer limited control over interfacial mixing and nanoparticle assembly, constraining both tunability and scalability. We present a hollow fiber membrane (HFM)-based platform that leverages dense arrays of nanoscale pores to mediate uniform, highly localized interfacial mixing, enabling controlled lipid self-assembly and RNA encapsulation. This nanopore-mediated architecture allows continuous, high-throughput synthesis of LNPs with tunable particle sizes, narrow size distributions, and high encapsulation efficiencies, with particle characteristics directly correlated to the membrane pore size. HFM-derived LNPs exhibit robust in vitro transfection and potent in vivo immune responses and are compatible with multiple lipid chemistries and nucleic acid payloads, including mRNA vaccine constructs. papers.abstract_zh: RNA 疗法正在重塑现代医学,COVID-19 大流行期间基于脂质纳米颗粒 (LNP) 的 mRNA 疫苗的快速部署就是例证。然而,大规模、可重复地生成具有精确定义的理化性质的 LNP 的能力仍然是一个严峻的挑战,特别是当颗粒尺寸和尺寸分布强烈影响生物分布、细胞摄取和治疗效果时。传统的混合技术可确保再现性,但对界面混合和纳米粒子组装的控制有限,限制了可调谐性和可扩展性。我们提出了一种基于中空纤维膜 (HFM) 的平台,该平台利用密集的纳米级孔阵列来介导均匀、高度局部的界面混合,从而实现受控的脂质自组装和 RNA 封装。这种纳米孔介导的结构允许连续、高通量合成具有可调粒径、窄粒径分布和高封装效率的 LNP,且颗粒特性与膜孔径直接相关。HFM 衍生的 LNP 表现出强大的体外转染和有效的体内免疫反应,并且与多种脂质化学和核酸有效负载(包括 mRNA 疫苗构建体)兼容。总之,这项工作将基于 HFM 的纳米孔组装确立为一种通用且可扩展的方法,用于生产明确的 LNP,与当前和未来的 mRNA 疫苗和治疗开发直接相关。

papers.title: Serological outcomes of SARS-CoV-2 infection by vaccination status and variant in England.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Throughout the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, several vaccines have been rolled out and distinct variants with different severity and immune profiles emerged in England. Using data from enhanced surveillance of COVID-19 in vaccine eligible individuals we investigated the antibody response following SARS-CoV-2 infection according to vaccination status and variant. METHODS: SARS-CoV-2 PCR-positive eligible individuals were identified from community PCR testing data in England between February 2021 and April 2022 and contacted by nurses to complete questionnaires at recruitment and 21 days post recruitment. Individuals were sent self-sampling kits and self-sampled nasal/oropharyngeal swabs were taken day 1, day 3 and day 7 post-recruitment as well as acute (day 1), convalescent (follow-up) serum and oral fluid samples. Regression analyses were used to investigate how N antibody seroconversion differs by vaccine status, and to investigate how N and S antibody levels differ by vaccine status overall and stratified by variants. Interval-censored analyses and regression analyses were used to investigate the effect of acute S antibody levels on the duration of positivity, the cycle threshold values, the self-reported symptom severity and the number of symptoms reported. RESULTS: A total of 1,497 PCR positive individuals were included. A total of 369 (24.7%) individuals were unvaccinated, 359 (24.0%) participants were infected with Alpha, 762 (50.9%) with Delta and 376 (25.2%) with Omicron. The median age of participants was 49 years old (IQR 39-57). Convalescent anti-N antibody levels were lower in vaccinated individuals and convalescent anti-S antibody levels were higher in vaccinated individuals and increased with the number of doses received. Acute anti-S antibody level increased with the number of doses received. Higher acute anti-S antibody levels were associated with a shorter duration of positivity (overall and for the Delta variant). Higher acute anti-S antibody levels were also associated with higher Ct values (overall and for the Alpha and Delta variants). There was no association between the acute anti-S antibody level and self-reported symptom severity. Individuals with higher acute anti-S antibody level were less likely to report six or more symptoms (overall and for Delta variant). CONCLUSION: Understanding the characteristics of the antibody response, its dynamics over time and the immunity it confers is important to inform future vaccination strategies and policies. Our findings suggest that vaccination is associated with high acute anti-S antibody level but reduced convalescent anti-N antibody level. High anti-S antibody level is associated with reduced duration of infection, reduced infectiousness and may also be associated with reduced symptoms severity and number of symptoms.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the public-health need to understand how SARS-CoV-2 vaccination and emerging variants shaped antibody responses after infection in England, where multiple vaccines were deployed and variants with distinct immune profiles circulated.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective enhanced surveillance study recruited PCR-positive, vaccine-eligible individuals in England between February 2021 and April 2022, collecting acute and convalescent sera, oral fluid, and self-sampled swabs at multiple time points.
analysis.methods: Participants completed questionnaires at recruitment and 21 days later; regression and interval-censored analyses were used to compare N and S antibody levels by vaccination status and variant, and to relate acute S antibody levels to duration of positivity, Ct values, and symptom profiles.
analysis.main_results: Among 1,497 PCR-positive individuals (median age 49 years), 24.7% were unvaccinated; 24.0% were infected with Alpha, 50.9% with Delta, and 25.2% with Omicron. Convalescent anti-N levels were lower in vaccinated individuals, while convalescent and acute anti-S levels rose with the number of vaccine doses.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that vaccination increases acute anti-S antibody levels and reduces convalescent anti-N levels, and that higher acute anti-S levels shorten infection duration and may lower infectiousness and symptom burden, highlighting implications for variant-specific immunity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings inform decisions on booster timing and variant-targeted vaccines by showing how prior vaccination modulates antibody kinetics and clinical outcomes after infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its observational design and reliance on self-reported symptoms and self-sampling, which may introduce bias; the evidence is assessed as moderate given the robust sampling framework but lack of randomization and potential unmeasured confounding.

analysis.summary_en: This prospective surveillance study in England followed 1,497 PCR-positive individuals from February 2021 to April 2022 to compare antibody responses after SARS-CoV-2 infection by vaccination status and variant. Vaccination was associated with higher acute and convalescent anti-S antibody levels and lower convalescent anti-N levels. Higher acute anti-S levels correlated with shorter infection duration and higher Ct values, suggesting reduced infectiousness, and were linked to fewer reported symptoms, though not to symptom severity. The authors conclude that understanding these antibody dynamics can guide future vaccination strategies, particularly for emerging variants.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项前瞻性强化监测研究于 2021 年 2 月至 2022 年 4 月期间在英格兰招募了 PCR 阳性、符合疫苗资格的个体,在多个时间点收集急性和恢复期血清、口腔液和自检拭子样本。
elements_zh.methods: 参与者在招募时和 21 天后完成了调查问卷;回归和区间删失分析用于根据疫苗接种状态和变异比较 N 和 S 抗体水平,并将急性 S 抗体水平与阳性持续时间、Ct 值和症状概况联系起来。
elements_zh.main_results: 在1,497名PCR阳性个体(中位年龄49岁)中,24.7%未接种疫苗;24.0%感染了Alpha变异株,50.9%感染了Delta变异株,25.2%感染了Omicron变异株。接种疫苗的个体恢复期抗N水平较低,而恢复期和急性抗S水平随疫苗剂量增加而上升。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,疫苗接种会增加急性抗 S 抗体水平并降低恢复期抗 N 水平,而较高的急性抗 S 水平会缩短感染持续时间,并可能降低传染性和症状负担,这凸显了对变异特异性免疫的影响。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现通过显示先前的疫苗接种如何调节感染后的抗体动力学和临床结果,为加强接种时机和变异靶向疫苗的决策提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其观察设计以及对自我报告症状和自我采样的依赖而受到限制,这可能会引入偏差;鉴于抽样框架稳健,但缺乏随机性和潜在的无法测量的混杂因素,证据被评估为中等。
